newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH ownership of DFS rises above 60 pct.
newsitem.headline: LVMH ownership of DFS rises above 60 pct.

text.p: French luxury goods group LVMH said on Monday that it controlled 61.25 percent of U.S. duty free chain DFS after one of the two shareholders who had fought the takeover, Anthony Pilaro, sold LVMH his 2.5 percent holding.
Pilaro obtained just over $100 million for his stake, the same price as the other shareholders who had previously sold LVMH 58.75 percent of DFS for $2.47 billion.
The last dissident shareholder, Robert Miller, holds 38.75 percent of DFS. Earlier this month, Miller said he and Pilaro had filed a lawsuit in New York seeking to reverse the takeover.
LVMH on Friday sold a third of its 21 percent stake in British drinks group Guinness Plc for around five billion francs, in part to help pay for the acquisition of DFS.
